# JavaScript and TypeScript

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-native-guides.py from docs/content. Do not edit this output. -->

GLRMask is a grammar-constrained decoding library for high-throughput LLM serving. It is optimized for fast mask computation with extremely low tail latency, even for complex grammars.

GLRMask supports general context-free grammars, including ambiguous ones. It accepts JSON Schema, Lark and [GLRM](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/glrm-format.md).

[Website](https://glrmask.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask) · [Paper](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23273556)

## Installation

`@glrmask/node` runs the GLRMask engine as a Node.js addon. It needs Node.js 22 or newer, and includes prebuilt binaries for Windows x64 and arm64, macOS x64 and arm64, and Linux x64 and arm64 (glibc or musl).

```sh
npm install @glrmask/node
```

The package provides CommonJS, ESM and TypeScript entry points.

## Usage

GLRMask has four core types:

- `Grammar`
- `Module`: a partially compiled grammar.
- `Constraint`: a compiled grammar, ready to use.
- `ConstraintState`: the state of one generated sequence.

## Quickstart

```js
import { Vocab, Grammar } from '@glrmask/node';

const grammar = Grammar.fromJsonSchema({
  type: 'object',
  properties: { color: { enum: ['red', 'green', 'blue'] } },
  required: ['color'],
  additionalProperties: false,
});

// One token per byte, plus EOS. With a real model, build this from its tokenizer.
const vocab = new Vocab(Array.from({ length: 256 }, (_, id) => [id, Uint8Array.of(id)]));
const EOS = 256;
const state = (await grammar.compile(vocab)).start();
const sample = Buffer.from('{"color": "blue"}');
const output = [];
while (true) {
  // Stand-in scores for a model that wants to produce sample.
  const logits = new Float32Array(257).fill(-1);
  logits[output.length < sample.length ? sample[output.length] : EOS] = 1;
  const mask = state.mask();
  let token = -1;
  for (let id = 0; id <= EOS; id++) {
    const allowed = id === EOS ? state.isAccepting()
      : ((mask[id >>> 5] >>> (id & 31)) & 1) === 1;
    if (allowed && (token < 0 || logits[id] > logits[token])) token = id;
  }
  if (token < 0) throw new Error('no allowed token and cannot stop');
  if (token === EOS) break;
  if (!state.commitToken(token)) throw new Error('allowed token rejected');
  output.push(token);
}
if (!state.isAccepting()) throw new Error("incomplete output");
console.log(Buffer.from(output).toString());
```

## Learn more

[Full guide](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/GUIDE.md) · [JavaScript API reference](https://glrmask.com/api/javascript/) · [Benchmarks](https://glrmask.com/#benchmarks)

## Vocabularies and token sets

`new Vocab(entries)` takes an iterable of `[id, bytes]` pairs (such as an array or Map), with each token's exact bytes as a `Uint8Array` or `Buffer`.
Use the bytes the tokenizer produces, not its display form: a token may be part of a UTF-8 character. IDs need not be
contiguous, and two tokens may have the same bytes. An ID can't appear twice. Leave out tokens with no bytes, such as
tool-call tokens; a token set can still allow them.

```js
const vocab = new Vocab([
  [0, Uint8Array.of(0xc3)],
  [1, Uint8Array.of(0xa9)],
  [2, Buffer.from('é')],
]);
```

`new TokenSet(ids)` is a set of token IDs, and
`TokenSet.fromRanges([{start, end}])` builds one from ranges that exclude `end`. See [token
sets](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/token-sets.md).

## Grammars

| Factory | Input |
| --- | --- |
| `Grammar.fromGlrm(source)` | [GLRM](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/glrm-format.md) |
| `Grammar.fromJsonSchema(schema)` | JSON Schema, as JSON text or a value |
| `Grammar.fromLark(source)` | [Lark](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/lark-dialect.md) |

## Composing grammars

```js
import { Vocab, Grammar, Module, Expr, Constraint } from '@glrmask/node';

const vocab = new Vocab(Array.from({ length: 256 }, (_, id) => [id, Uint8Array.of(id)]));
const weather = new Module(Grammar.fromJsonSchema({
  type: 'object',
  properties: { city: { type: 'string' } },
  required: ['city'],
  additionalProperties: false,
}));
await weather.precompile(vocab);

const call = new Module(Grammar.fromGlrm(`
  extern grammar ARGS
  start call
  nt call = "<weather>" ARGS "</weather>"
`));
call.bind('ARGS', weather);
const constraint = await call.compile(vocab);
```

On a Module, `bind(name, value)` takes a `Grammar`, `Module`, `Expr`, or `TokenSet`. `bind` changes the module in place, so `clone()` it first to bind the
same one in different ways. `externs.unbound` lists the unbound names.

`Expr.choice(...parts)`, `Expr.sequence(...parts)` and `Expr.literal(text)` combine grammars without writing a new one:

```js
const reply = Expr.choice(Grammar.fromLark('start: "yes"'), Grammar.fromLark('start: "no"'));
const grammar = Grammar.fromExpr(Expr.sequence(Expr.literal('Answer: '), reply));
```

Grammar expressions must not contain modules, constraints or token sets, even indirectly. Bind model-specific values on a Module.

## Mask strategies

`compile` and `precompile` take `{maskStrategy}`.

| `MaskStrategy` | Value | Preference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Auto` | `'auto'` | The default; currently `FastMasks`. |
| `FastCompile` | `'fast-compile'` | Faster compilation, slower masks. |
| `FastMasks` | `'fast-masks'` | Faster masks, slower compilation. |

These are preferences, not speed guarantees.
See [mask strategies](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/GUIDE.md#mask-strategies).

## Generating

```js
const state = constraint.start();
const mask = new Uint32Array(Math.ceil(constraint.maskBitLength / 32));
state.fillMask(mask);
const allowed = (id) => ((mask[id >>> 5] >>> (id & 31)) & 1) === 1;
```

A mask contains packed uint32 words: token i is bit i % 32 of word Math.floor(i / 32).
`fillMask` writes it into an array you reuse; `mask()` returns a new one.

`commitToken` and `commitBytes` consume the input. They return true if the state is viable after the commit (this does not imply it is accepting); false means the state is dead, not that the commit was rolled back. A dead state is not accepting, is terminated, has an all-zero mask and empty forced bytes, and every later non-empty commit returns false. A dead state can also arise from a grammar whose language is empty. To try input without risking the state, clone it first. Committing empty bytes leaves the state unchanged and returns whether it is viable. Commit special tokens and token sets with `commitToken`;
bytes never match them.

`isAccepting()` says whether the output so far could end here, and `isTerminated()` whether nothing more can be
committed. `forcedBytes()` returns the bytes that must come next. Tokenize and commit them yourself; exact token-set items are not included.

[examples/generate.mjs](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/bindings/node/examples/generate.mjs) is a
complete generation loop.

## Async and sync

`compile`, `precompile`, `save` and `load` return promises and run off the main thread. `compileSync`, `precompileSync`,
`saveSync` and `loadSync` do the same work and block. Everything else is synchronous.

An async call works on a snapshot of its inputs, so changing or disposing them afterwards doesn't affect it. If a module
is bound while its `precompile` is running, the promise rejects; precompile it again.

## Saving

```js
const bytes = await constraint.save();
const restored = await Constraint.load(bytes, vocab);

const moduleBytes = await call.save();
const module = await Module.load(moduleBytes);
```

Saved bytes are the same in every binding, so a constraint saved from Python loads in Node. A saved constraint doesn't
include its vocabulary: pass the same vocabulary to `load`, which checks that it matches exactly. A saved module records
the vocabulary its precompiled parts were built for; `compile` and `precompile` check it. Saved bytes are only guaranteed to load in
the same GLRMask version on the same architecture, so keep the grammar source to compile again after an upgrade. Don't
load saved bytes from untrusted sources.

Empty ranges are no-ops; reversed ranges are invalid. Bindings capture their values. Stop decisions belong to the caller: committing an unknown EOS rejects the state even if it was accepting.

## Errors

Arguments of the wrong type throw `TypeError`. Native GLRMask errors throw a
`GLRMaskError`. The message text is for humans; its format is not stable. Its `code` is one of:

| Code | |
| --- | --- |
| `GLRMASK_SYNTAX` | Invalid grammar syntax. |
| `GLRMASK_INVALID_INPUT` | A handle or argument is invalid. |
| `GLRMASK_COMPILATION` | Compilation failed. |
| `GLRMASK_RESOURCE_LIMIT` | A resource limit was exceeded. |
| `GLRMASK_STRATEGY_UNSUPPORTED` | The chosen strategy does not support the grammar. |
| `GLRMASK_SERIALIZATION` | Saved bytes could not be loaded. |
| `GLRMASK_VOCAB_MISMATCH` | Compiled for a different vocabulary. |
| `GLRMASK_INTERNAL` | An internal error; discard the affected object and please report it. |
| `GLRMASK_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` | The array passed to `fillMask` is shorter than `Math.ceil(maskBitLength / 32)`. |
| `GLRMASK_CLOSED` | The object was disposed. |

A lost asynchronous precompile race reports `GLRMASK_PRECOMPILE_RACE`. Async methods reject with the same errors. Out-of-u32 commit arguments raise RangeError without changing the state.

## Freeing memory

Objects hold native memory, freed when they are garbage collected. `dispose()`, or a `using` declaration, frees it
straight away. Disposing twice is harmless. A state keeps its constraint alive, so disposing the constraint doesn't affect
states already started.

## API reference

[index.d.cts](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/bindings/node/index.d.cts) documents every class and method.
CommonJS and ESM export the same API.

## Building from source

You need Node.js 22 or newer, a stable Rust toolchain, and a C/C++ compiler. On Windows, use a Visual Studio Developer
PowerShell with the MSVC build tools.

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix bindings/node
npm run build --prefix bindings/node
```

`npm run build` puts the compiled addon next to the package's loader, where it takes priority over an installed platform
package. `npm pack --prefix bindings/node` makes a package you can install elsewhere. A build runs only on the platform it
was built for.
